subject: Crescendo Labs renewal: commit rebalance, rate shelter & credit request
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@crescendolabs.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jason Moore <j.moore@crescendolabs.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal intake — capacity uplift + temporary rate shelter

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding help in Q1. We're starting our renewal conversations internally and wanted to surface a couple of asks early so procurement can budget:

- We need committed capacity increased from 150M tokens/month to ~350M tokens/month beginning 6/1. Burst must be supported for Black Friday style campaigns but average will be steady-state.
- Because of headcount-led product launches, we need price predictability: can Redwood provide a 12-month rate shelter (cap on per-token rate) even if we increase commit?
- To get finance to sign, we may need a one-time credit applied to the first invoice and a phased true-up schedule.

I've attached a short workbook with current usage slices and our proposed commit ladder (Renewal_Request_0412.xlsx). Our procurement window is tight — expectation is to finalize T&Cs by end of May.

Can we schedule a 30–45 minute call this week to get concrete options? Jason and I are available Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Best,
Ellen Park
VP, Platform Engineering
Crescendo Labs

[attachment: Renewal_Request_0412.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@crescendolabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal intake — capacity uplift + temporary rate shelter

Ellen — thanks for the workbook and the clear ask. Appreciate getting this early visibility.

High level options we can bring to the table on a call:
1) Commit Rebalance + 12-month Rate Cap: move to 350M tokens/month committed with a 12-month per-token cap. This requires an 18-month minimum commitment period (so we can absorb the capacity scheduling cost). We can offer a front-loaded credit to assist transition.
2) Staged Uplift + Quarterly True-ups: stagger the commit (200M -> 350M over 3 quarters) with smaller credits tied to milestone usage. This is more flexible for you but slightly higher unit price.
3) Dedicated Pool + Burst Insurance: keep commit lower, add a dedicated burst pool (reserved burst capacity) for holiday traffic and an insurance credit to protect monthly spend variance.

Ben has a quick note on the infra implications (see his reply).

I'm free Wed 10:00–11:00 PST or Thu 09:00–10:00 PST — will book a slot once you confirm.

Attaching a short options doc I can share with finance/legal so we have something firm to react to (Proposed_Pricing_Options_v1.pdf).

Thanks,
Priyom
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[attachment: Proposed_Pricing_Options_v1.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@crescendolabs.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal intake — capacity uplift + temporary rate shelter

Ellen — quick technical / ops context to help the pricing convo:

- Moving to a 350M committed baseline is straightforward from a runtime perspective. We recommend a mixed strategy: increased commit for steady-state, plus a dedicated burst pool sized at ~50–75M tokens/month equivalent to accommodate peak traffic.
- Prefetching and prefix KV caching will reduce effective token load for repeat conversational flows; expect ~10–18% effective savings depending on your prompt patterns. We'll model those savings into the final unit price.
- If you need the 12-month cap, that impacts how we amortize GPU allocation and reserved capacity; that’s why Priyom suggested an 18-month minimum commit so we can offer a heavier credit.

Happy to jump on the call to walk through numbers and latency/throughput SLAs.

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal intake — capacity uplift + temporary rate shelter (approval request)

Laur — forwarding Crescendo's ask and our options. Quick summary for legal/finance approvals:

- Proposed commercial: 350M tokens/month committed, 18-month minimum term, 12-month rate shelter on per-token rate, one-time signing credit of $75,000 applied to first invoice.
- Condition: if customer terminates before 18 months, credit recoupment on a pro-rata basis over remaining months.
- Ops note: dedicated burst pool recommended; modeling shows ~12% token efficiency with KV/prefix caching that we should bake into unit price.

Can legal draft an amendment that captures the rate shelter, the recoupment schedule, and a clear SLA on burst provisioning? Finance: are we ok with the $75k credit given model/ARR targets for the quarter? I attached a draft SOW for scope and timing.

If you can greenlight language and budget, I'll move to a formal quote and ask Crescendo to sign DocuSign by May 28 to meet their procurement window.

Thanks — Priyom

[attachment: SOW_Draft_Crescendo.docx (docx, 48KB)]

From: Jason Moore <j.moore@crescendolabs.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@crescendolabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal intake — capacity uplift + temporary rate shelter

Priyom — thanks to you and Ben for the options and the draft SOW. Wed 10am PST works for us (confirming the slot).

Two quick asks ahead of the call so we can bring procurement and legal to the meeting:
1) Can you share a simple one-page commercial: committed quantity, proposed per-token cap, credit amount, commit term, and early-termination recoup schedule (we'll use that for our finance review)?
2) If you can include a timeline for migration/validation (how long to ramp burst pool and do a smoke test), that will help our release planning.

If we can get that one-pager and a tentative DocuSign quote after the call, procurement expects to complete sign-off by 5/26. Deal id for our internal tracking: CR-2026-089.

Looking forward to the call.

—Jason
Director, Infrastructure & Procurement
Crescendo Labs
